so what? phrase

also what then?, and then?, what of it?, and so?, what next?, and then what?

classical

Plaut. Curc. 726: Quid tum?
Cic. Tusc. 2.26 (Lewis & Short)

Quid tum?

so what? what then? and then?

It either asks for the rest of the story or challenges the point of what was said.

Other words

  • Quid tum posteā? — and what then? what of it?

    also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 346b: Quid tum posteā?

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • Nōvī ego hōs pugnōs meōs. — Quid tum? — Quid tum, rogitās? Hīsce ego, sī tū mē irrītāveris, placidum tē hodiē reddam.

    I know these fists of mine. — So what? — So what, you ask? If you provoke me, I’ll use them to make you a quiet man today.Plaut. Curc. 725c–727

  • Quid tum? — Auscultā ergō, scīēs.

    And then? — Listen, then, and you’ll find out.Plaut. Asin. 350b–350c

See also then, why so?, what’s the matter?, what?!.

SourcesLewis & Short: quis · Lewis & Short: tum

Plautus, Asinaria 346b, 350b–350c; Curculio 725c–727.
